rationale: Both candidates ground findings in real code paths, but Y lands much closer to the actual reviewer thread: it independently reconstructs gcanlin's architectural objection to reading cudagraph_mode in modeling (comment 1, even proposing the exact runner-side fix that would let the TODO be deleted), precisely nails the seed-reproducibility regression gcanlin warned about (and sharpens it by showing CUDAGraphWrapper replay drops seeds at every batch size, not just >1), and connects talker_mtp_graph_safe=True being false on NPU to the real Wallbreazzz crash plus the failing NPU/AMD CI gates. X's findings (prefix-cache/async interaction, docs staleness, missing unit tests) are plausible but mostly tangential to what reviewers actually flagged, and it restates the same async/prefix-cache point twice, diluting precision. Y's comments also carry more concrete, root-cause-targeted code suggestions rather than generic 'add a test/doc' asks.
